work_items.title: Traffic Analytics and Live Active-User Counter
work_items.summary: Prepare Web-first privacy-safe historical traffic and ephemeral active-presence measurement, with a shared contract for future Fitness and Mazer reuse.
work_items.objective: Define truthful traffic and active-now measurements and an internal-facing view with explicit privacy, freshness, provider, and product acceptance boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Specify the Web-first historical traffic and active-now product outcome, with future Fitness/Mazer reuse documented as a shared measurement contract rather than separate duplicate Web-parent cards.

2. Define visitor, page-view, session, registered-account, active-product-user and active-now terms, units, deduplication rules and time zones so labels cannot imply that concurrent sessions equal people or account totals.
3. Show privacy-safe visitor totals for today, trailing 7 days and trailing 30 days, with explicit aggregation and unavailable/stale states.
4. Show page views and popular pages from canonical safe routes, with a stated treatment of redirects, bots and repeated views.
5. Show referrer summaries only where privacy policy and the selected source permit them; avoid raw identifying URL or query values.
6. Show aggregate device/browser trends only at a safe granularity and suppress or omit small/private segments as required by the approved public/private policy.
7. Provide an active-now total and per-app counts under one consistent contract, initially for Web and extendable to Fitness/Mazer, without treating registered accounts as active presence.

8. Count visible active sessions from an authoritative presence snapshot with explicit expiry, disconnect, reconnect and cross-tab behavior; recalculate from current state rather than accumulating join/leave deltas as a durable counter.

9. Deduplicate an authenticated user across active connections where appropriate and an anonymous browser within its permitted session scope. Define exactly what is counted when user identity is unavailable; publish no presence identities.

10. Keep presence payloads minimal and ephemeral. Exclude names, email, IP, precise location, raw user agents, private routes, free-form text and other personally identifying information from the displayed counts and client-visible state.

11. Keep provider credentials and privileged Supabase access server-only. Any browser read uses an authorized, sanitized aggregate interface with explicit access policy and no direct private board-table exposure.

12. Reconcile the already-written first-party analytics source and its closed event vocabulary with the proposed Vercel option, including whether existing data can supply the requested history and which single source is authoritative for each metric. Provider setup, cost and retention remain separate decisions.

13. Deliver an internal-facing view and verify count accuracy, freshness, resilience to presence churn, privacy, accessibility and narrow-screen presentation with realistic multi-session cases. A public badge is optional only after its own validation and approval.

14. Return source, integration, release and product acceptance evidence separately. Do not mark the card complete from local source, a preview, an analytics dashboard screenshot, or a deployed count without the corresponding approved live readback and receiving proof.
discoveries: The live online-now display (criteria 7 to 10) shipped on its own as FW-PRESENCE-001 using an anonymous live channel; nothing here has been built for historical traffic.
Fitness FF-ANALYTICS-001 and FF-SOC-002 are related distinct outcomes; their identities, dependencies, and acceptance remain with Fitness.
The collected page views live in a table only the service role can read, with no visitor or session id and no read path, so totals, popular pages and referrers need new database work.
next_actions: Decide whether traffic numbers are worth building, and whether they would be public or owner-only.
If yes: design a read path over the collected page views (a database function or an Edge GET) for the owner's approval; no identifiers are collected today.
blockers: Needs the owner's decision and approval of a database read path over the collected page views, plus the public or owner-only decision for traffic numbers.

work_items.title: Add a bot check to the sign-in, sign-up and reset forms
work_items.summary: Add a bot check to the account forms before public launch, using a free provider that the account backend supports natively.
work_items.objective: Keep automated abuse out of the account forms without adding friction for most people.
acceptance_criteria: The sign-in, sign-up and reset forms show the provider widget and send its result with each request.
The account backend verifies the result and rejects requests without a valid one.
The forms stay usable on narrow screens and with keyboard-only input.
Turning the check on is a separate, approved provider-settings step with a rollback.
next_actions: Create the provider widget for the account site and record its public site identifier.
Add the widget to the three forms in one reviewed change, behind the provider-settings step.
Verify sign-in, sign-up and reset end to end on a phone and a desktop browser.
blockers: Needs a captcha provider account and its site key and secret, and the account backend's captcha setting switched on. Those are credentials and a provider setting only the owner can create.

work_items.title: Check the account pages and project boards on a real phone
work_items.summary: The account pages and the public project boards were checked on a real phone on 2026-11-13: nothing looked off. Reported by the owner; not independently observed.
work_items.objective: Confirm sign-in, sign-out, the account pages and the project boards behave on an actual phone, including the home-screen app.
acceptance_criteria: Sign-in, sign-out and the Fitness handoff work on a real phone.
The four project-board tabs and card details open, scroll and close without layout breaks.
Findings are recorded and any fix ships through the normal reviewed path.
discoveries: Owner report, 2026-11-13: sign-in, sign-out, the four board tabs and the account pages looked right on a phone.
next_actions: Repeat the pass after any large change to the account pages or the boards.

work_items.title: Make Projects owner-only and check it live
work_items.summary: The Projects tab and page are for the signed-in account owner only. The static site ships no board data; a server endpoint verifies the owner and returns every card. It still needs a real-device check by the owner.
work_items.objective: Show every project card to the owner and nobody else, without per-card hiding.
acceptance_criteria: Signed-out visitors and every other account see no Projects tab and receive no board data.
The signed-in owner sees the tab and all boards at the account origin.
The built static site contains no board card text.
The owner view is checked on a real device.
discoveries: The owner endpoint needs the server-only owner list setting; without it the page fails closed and shows nothing, for everyone.
Pages on the main site show the Projects link only while a harmless hint cookie set by the account site is present; the account page still verifies the owner on the server.
next_actions: Sign in as the owner on a phone and check the tab and every board.
Sign in as another account and signed out to confirm nothing shows.

work_items.title: Show a live online-now count in the site header
work_items.summary: The site header shows how many people are on the website right now, in place of the brand text: a dim dot, then a count once connected. It counts visible site tabs through an anonymous live connection that stores nothing and needs no database change. Checked live in desktop Chrome with two browsers (1, then 2, then 1) and at phone widths; not checked on a real phone. Historical traffic, referrers and per-app counts stay on FW-ANALYTICS-001.
work_items.objective: Give a truthful, privacy-safe live count that never shows a made-up number.
acceptance_criteria: The header shows a dim dot when the count is unknown and a number only for a real positive count.
The count is recomputed from the current presence snapshot and counts each visible tab once.
Nothing identifying is sent or stored, and the privacy page says so.
It runs only on the production site origins and is loaded after the page settles.
The header looks right on a real phone.
discoveries: The channel is public, so anyone with the public key could inflate the number; treat it as a casual indicator.
Realtime connection quotas on the shared project apply; past them the display goes dim.
next_actions: Look at the header on a real phone once.
Decide whether a per-browser count and a traffic view belong to FW-ANALYTICS-001.
